title.narrative: UNICEF’s financial and technical support to Government for the cholera and El Niño response provided safe water services to 480,262 people through emergency water point rehabilitation and solar-powered piped systems. UNICEF also delivered critical non-food items, including WASH hygiene kits, to over 2.2 million individuals in cholera-affected areas via community campaigns and media. UNICEF collaborated with and strengthened government agencies at various levels to manage cholera outbreaks while also co-leading the WASH sector throughout the response leading to a declaration of the end of the cholera outbreak by August 2024.Through strategic partnerships with Vitens Evides International (VEI), UNICEF was able to boost service delivery capacity of urban local authorities for large cities like Harare and Bulawayo. UNICEF also participated in the Government led cholera intra and after action reviews and helped shape the WASH priorities that are being implemented in the current cholera response.
